findings.title: Lithuanian message replaced with Italian text
findings.body: In the Lithuanian account bundle line 101 totpStep1 is now 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian sentence in the account console. The change was meant to remove <a> links, but copied the Italian translation instead of a Lithuanian one.

findings.title: Lithuanian login message replaced with Italian text
findings.body: In the Lithuanian login bundle line 71 loginTotpStep1 is now 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' which is Italian. Users with Lithuanian locale will see Italian instructions on the TOTP setup page. This is the same copy-paste error as in the account bundle.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese file uses Traditional characters
findings.body: In the zh_CN account bundle line 112 totpStep1 is now 'In your mobile install one of the following apps' written with Traditional characters (手機, 應用程式, 安裝). The file is Simplified Chinese which should use 手机, 应用程序, 安装. Simplified-Chinese users will see the wrong script variant.

findings.title: Diff snippet can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
findings.body: When sanitized and original values differ, the code strips common prefix (start) and suffix (end) then does value.substring(start, value.length()-end). It never checks that start+end does not exceed the length. If the common prefix and suffix overlap the substring bounds are inverted and substring throws, aborting verification with an exception instead of reporting illegal HTML.

findings.title: Throws RuntimeException instead of MojoExecutionException on read failure
findings.body: verifySafeHtml wraps failure to read the checked file and failure to read the English reference file in RuntimeException. The public verify() contract is MojoExecutionException for IO problems. A missing English file therefore crashes the Maven plugin with an unchecked exception and stack trace instead of a clean Mojo failure.

findings.title: PropertyResourceBundle with InputStream misdecodes UTF-8
findings.body: The verifier loads message bundles with new PropertyResourceBundle(new FileInputStream(file)), which decodes as ISO-8859-1. The message files contain raw UTF-8 (Arabic, Chinese, Lithuanian, etc.), so non-ASCII values are mojibake when inspected. Error reports will show garbled text and all comparisons run on corrupted strings. It should use the Reader constructor with UTF-8.

findings.title: Stray 'n' left in Danish email HTML
findings.body:
In the Danish email bundle line 9 identityProviderLinkBodyHtml contains '

nHvis du ikke vil...' with an extra leading n, while the plain-text version has correct 'Hvis'. Recipients will see a paragraph starting with 'nHvis'. The PR fixed the missing

but left the typo.

findings.title: Stray 'n' left in Lithuanian email HTML
findings.body:
In the Lithuanian email bundle line 3 emailVerificationBodyHtml contains '

nJei paskyros...' with an extra leading n, while the plain-text version has correct 'Jei'. Recipients will see a paragraph starting with 'nJei'.

findings.title: Anchor mismatch message lacks key and file
findings.body: When a translated anchor does not exactly match the English anchor the verifier adds "Didn't find anchor tag ... in original string" with no key name and no file name, unlike the Illegal HTML message which includes both. When run over hundreds of bundles this failure is unactionable and requires manual search to locate.

findings.title: No positive test that valid HTML passes
findings.body: All tests assert that bad fixtures produce a message with hasItem, but there is no test asserting that a valid translation with allowed tags or identical anchors produces zero messages. A false positive in the sanitizer would therefore go unnoticed, and the duplicate-keys test would still pass even with extra spurious errors.
